parts.technique: Integration by parts of x ln(3x) type function, definite integral
parts.reason: P8.5 covers integration by parts as inverse of product rule, including cases requiring the integral ln x dx; this integral by parts with algebraic/log integrand fits directly.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Connected rates of change (dV/dt, dx/dt) via chain rule
parts.reason: P7.4 guidance explicitly mentions connected rates of change in models, e.g. dV/dt = dV/dr x dr/dt; this is the same technique applied to a cube.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Evaluate connected rate at given value
parts.reason: Direct continuation of part (a)'s in-spec connected rates method, substituting a value.

parts.technique: Separable first order differential equation with particular solution
parts.reason: P8.7 explicitly covers solving separable first order differential equations including finding particular solutions using given initial conditions.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Binomial expansion of (a+bx)^n for rational n
parts.reason: P4.1 explicitly extends binomial expansion to any rational n including use for approximation, matching (4+5x)^(1/2) type expansion.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: State range of validity of binomial expansion
parts.reason: P4.1 explicitly states awareness that expansion is valid for |bx/a|<1 and students may be asked to comment on range of validity.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Use binomial expansion result to derive expansion of (4-5x)^(1/2) and combine two expansions
parts.reason: Extension of the in-spec binomial expansion technique (P4.1), applying substitution symmetry and combining series - standard use of same expansion skill.

parts.technique: Implicit differentiation to find tangent to a curve
parts.reason: P7.5 explicitly requires differentiating functions defined implicitly (first derivative only) and finding tangents/normals to curves given implicitly.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Parametric differentiation to find gradient
parts.reason: P7.5 explicitly covers differentiating functions defined parametrically for the first derivative, including finding tangents/normals.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Find normal to parametric curve and its intersection with x-axis using algebra
parts.reason: Direct continuation of P7.5's parametric differentiation and finding equations of tangents/normals to curves given parametrically.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Convert parametric equations to Cartesian form
parts.reason: P3.3 explicitly covers conversion between Cartesian and parametric forms of curves.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Integration by substitution (given substitution) to transform an integral
parts.reason: P8.5 explicitly covers integration by substitution including finding a suitable substitution, matching the given substitution transformation task.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Decompose rational function into partial fractions (denominator with squared linear term, 3 terms)
parts.reason: P2.10 explicitly covers partial fractions with denominators such as (ax+b)(cx+d)^2, matching u^2(2u+1) form.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Integrate using partial fractions (linear in denominator) and evaluate definite integral after substitution
parts.reason: P8.6 covers integrating using partial fractions linear in the denominator, combined with P8.2/P8.3 for definite integral evaluation; fully in-spec technique chain.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Find vector AB and vector equation of a line through two points
parts.reason: P10.4 covers position vectors and finding vector between two points; P10.1-10.3 cover vector equations of lines using position vectors and direction vectors.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Use perpendicularity of vectors (dot product = 0) to find unknown component
parts.reason: Perpendicular vectors via scalar (dot) product is a standard vector technique; while dot product isn't explicitly named, P10.5 covers using vectors to solve problems and this is a natural extension of vector operations covered under P10.3/P10.5.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Find area of triangle from vectors (via magnitude of cross product or equivalent trig method)
parts.reason: Main mark scheme method uses vector cross product (not explicitly named in any P10 statement), but an alternative full-marks method uses magnitudes of CA, CB and the angle between them via cos^-1 of the dot-product ratio, then area = 1/2 ab sin C, which relies only on magnitude/vector operations covered by P10.2-P10.5 and P5.1, so full marks achievable via in-spec method.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Volume of revolution using algebraic integration (log integration)
parts.reason: P8.3 covers definite integrals for finding areas/volumes as an application of integration, combined with P8.2's ln f(x) integration form for the given rational function.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Solve equation involving logs/exponentials derived from integral expression for unknown depth
parts.reason: Continuation of the integration technique in (a) plus solving log/exponential equations (P6.3/P6.4), both in-spec.

parts.technique: Proof by contradiction involving parity argument on integers
parts.reason: P1.1 explicitly lists proof by contradiction as a required method with guidance/examples including deduction via even/odd arguments; this matches the structure required (assume p^2-4q+2=0, derive parity contradiction).
